headlines.title: 4 arrested in shooting of 49ers player Keion White at San Francisco nightclub
headlines.description: Four suspects have been arrested in connection with the February shooting of San Francisco 49ers player Keion White at a Mission District nightclub, San Francisco officials announced Wednesday. The arrests were made in various cities across California and Georgia following a monthslong investigation that included more than 50 search warrants and assistance from over 250 law enforcement personnel, officials said. White, a defensive lineman for the 49ers, was shot in the early morning hours of Feb. 9 at a nightclub located on the 1700 block of Mission Street, according to police. “It started when multiple suspects, some brandishing firearms, confronted the 49ers player, which then led to a physical altercation between the group and the victim, who was shot in the leg,” San Francisco police Chief Derrick Lew said. White has since recovered following surgery and has been playing for the 49ers this season. Keion White May 2 Ricky Pearsall Sep 19, 2025 Following several months of investigation, officers last week served four no-bail arrest warrants. Atlanta police arrested 38-year-old Marquis Davis at his home last Wednesday. Officers found an illegal firearm, 820 grams of MDMA, 1,026 grams of methamphetamine, 979 grams of cocaine and 3,842 grams of fentanyl, police said. Later that morning, San Francisco police and San Joaquin County sheriff’s deputies arrested 36-year-old Antoine Washington in Stockton. Officers recovered a loaded firearm, more than 120 oxycodone pills and roughly $7,000, according to police. In Southern California on the same day, San Francisco police and Irvine police took 35-year-old Curtis Green into custody without incident. The fourth suspect, 36-year-old Gregory Walker of Mountain House, was arrested last Friday in Los Angeles for his alleged involvement in the shooting, police said. Walker has since been charged with assault with a firearm with allegations that he personally discharged that firearm at White, San Francisco District Attorney Brooke Jenkins said. Walker was also charged with possession of a firearm by a felon, possession of a concealed firearm by a felon and possession of a loaded firearm by a felon. Jenkins said the district attorney’s office filed a motion to keep Walker in custody because they believe he poses a public safety risk. His arraignment is scheduled to take place Wednesday afternoon. Green faces multiple misdemeanors, including brandishing a firearm and carrying a concealed weapon, Jenkins said. “We will not tolerate any type of violence in our city, but certainly not gun violence,” Jenkins said. “We had a great, amazing Super Bowl weekend that ended with this incident. I am just so thankful to the San Francisco police that we are being able to hold those accountable who sadly chose violence on that night.” San Francisco police are working with the district attorney’s office and prosecutors in other jurisdictions to arrange for Davis and Washington to be transferred to the city to face charges, Lew said. The February shooting marked the second time in two years that a 49ers player was shot in the city. Wide receiver Ricky Pearsall was shot and injured during an alleged attempted robbery in Union Square in August 2024. He made a full recovery. NBC News contributed to this report.

headlines.title: Netflix to cut about 6% of worldwide staff
headlines.description: Netflix is eliminating about 6% of its employee roster, or roughly 1,000 jobs, in a round of layoffs announced internally Wednesday, according to a source with knowledge of the matter. “Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” Netflix co-chief executives Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos said in an email to staff members Wednesday. The news was first reported by The Wall Street Journal. The source with knowledge of the matter confirmed the newspaper’s reporting was accurate. Netflix remains one of the titans of streaming, but it has struggled to boost user engagement on the platform. The service’s users watched more than 97 billion hours of content in the first half of 2026, an increase of 2% year-over-year, according to the company’s most recent quarterly earnings report. “Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster,” Sarandos said at Bloomberg’s annual media conference late last month. Netflix is expected to report its third-quarter financial results next Tuesday. The majority of the job cuts will be concentrated in Netflix’s product, technology, legal and human-resources teams. Peters and Sarandos said the streaming firm will “continue to invest aggressively in high impact areas” while also “making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees and investors.” In recent months, Netflix has looked for ways to boost subscriber engagement, including adding live sports programming and video podcasts licensed from third-party companies such as Bill Simmons’ The Ringer. Netflix’s layoffs come as other major Hollywood studios look to reduce costs and streamline operations. The Walt Disney Co. has cut hundreds of jobs this year under new Chief Executive Josh D’Amaro, according to a source familiar with the matter. David Ellison’s Skydance is widely expected to shrink its work force across Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery.

headlines.title: Bay Area faces fire weather concerns as temperatures rise
headlines.description: Warmer temperatures and dry conditions are expected across the Bay Area through Friday, raising fire weather concerns in higher elevations, particularly in the North Bay interior mountains, according to the National Weather Service. Moderate offshore winds are expected, with the strongest winds projected for Thursday, increasing the risk of fires spreading quickly if a fire starts. Temperatures will continue to rise through the end of the workweek, with the warmest conditions expected Friday. Inland areas could reach the mid-80s to mid-90s, while parts of the Peninsula and Santa Cruz Mountains could see highs in the upper 80s to mid-90s. The forecast led PG&E to notify more than 11,000 customers in the North and East Bay that they may have their power shut off between Wednesday evening and Saturday to avoid sparking wildfires. The power outages, which PG&E calls Public Safety Power Shutoffs, are expected to affect about 70,000 customers in 29 counties across the utility’s service range. In the Bay Area, that includes an estimated 4,705 in Alameda County, 1,605 in Contra Costa County, 3,027 in Napa County, 30 in Solano County, and 1,783 in Sonoma County. Meanwhile, a Coastal Flood Advisory remains in effect through 4 p.m. Wednesday for bayshore locations along San Pablo Bay. High tides could flood low-lying areas, cause isolated road closures and increase coastal erosion. PG&E 20 hours ago Microclimate Forecast 19 hours ago Forecast: Warmer ahead

headlines.title: Power outage affects hundreds in downtown Novato
headlines.description: A power outage is affecting downtown Novato on Wednesday morning, according to PG&E and local police. The outage was reported at 8:44 a.m. and is affecting 912 customers. PG&E on its outage map website said power is not expected to be restored until 6:45 p.m. Novato police said traffic signals are out in the area affected by the outage, and drivers should treat those intersections like ones with four-way stop signs. No information about what caused the outage was immediately available. The outage was unrelated to PG&E’s Public Safety Power Shutoffs planned for more than 11,000 customers in the North and East Bay starting Wednesday evening and going through Saturday to avoid sparking wildfires during dry and windy weather.

headlines.title: South Bay woman dies after car plunges off parking garage in Hawaii
headlines.description: A South Bay woman died last Friday after her car plunged five stories off a parking garage in Hawaii. The deadly plunge happened at a condominium complex in Honolulu. Investigators said the car, driven by an 84-year-old woman from San Jose, crashed through a retaining wall and fell about five stories before landing on the sidewalk below. Investigators were trying to figure out what led up to the crash. No one else was hurt.

headlines.title: Santa Rosa police arrest woman for alleged attempted child abduction
headlines.description: Officers in Santa Rosa arrested a woman on suspicion of attempted child abduction earlier this week, police said. On Monday just after 8 a.m., officers received a report regarding a mother walking with her young children when she was confronted by another woman. The mother was in the 700 block of Seventh Street with her toddler and a 10-month-old baby when an unknown woman aggressively approached them and prevented them from leaving the area, the Santa Rosa Police Department said in a statement Tuesday. The suspect allegedly demanded access to the baby, who was strapped into a stroller. The woman said she was going to take the child and reached into the stroller, grabbing at the baby. She then allegedly pulled on the stroller and continued to make statements about taking the baby. The mother called out for help, and a passing motorist stopped to help. The suspect fled the area before officers arrived. Neither child suffered physical injury. On Tuesday, detectives found a photo of a person of interest that was captured by an area security camera. At about 1:10 p.m., an officer saw a woman matching the photograph in the area of Second and D streets. The woman was arrested on suspicion of attempted kidnapping, child endangerment, and violating her pretrial release. Police believe the same suspect approached a woman walking her dog on Slater Street, where the suspect allegedly challenged the woman unprovoked and followed her.

headlines.title: SJ landlord killed by police after opening fire during tenant dispute on Locke Drive
headlines.description: A landlord-tenant dispute in South San Jose turned deadly Sunday night when a 69-year-old man was shot and killed by police following an exchange of gunfire. The series of events unfolded Sunday night, starting with an argument between the suspect and his tenant over rent and household guests. According to San Jose Police Chief Paul Joseph, “Initial reports of the confrontation describe the landlord as having a handgun in his pants pocket as he repeatedly pushed a guest of a tenant.” The suspect was identified as 69-year-old Ted Lieu. Police were initially unable to determine if a crime had occurred, and the victims did not want to pursue charges, so officers left the scene. However, about an hour later, the same tenant called 911 again. Chief Joseph said the caller “reported that the landlord was standing in the hallway of the house holding a shotgun threatening her and preventing her and another roommate from leaving the residence.” When police arrived, they found that Lieu had fled the location. Officers safely removed the victims from the home and began searching the area, locating Lieu hiding in a shed just a few houses down. Investigators say he ultimately opened fire. “During the encounter with the armed suspect it appears based on early stages of evidence processing that he discharged at least one round in the direction of officers,” Chief Joseph said. Three officers returned fire, and Lieu was pronounced dead at the scene. During the investigation, a firearm was recovered, alongside an assault rifle found at the suspect’s residence and a third firearm discovered in a garbage can. Investigators noted that Lieu had a history of conflict with neighbors and tenants involving firearms, as well as a prior history with law enforcement. The shock of the incident is still settling in for residents along Locke Drive. “It breaks our heart and right now our whole street is very concerned, very sad about the situation, what’s happening; I never would have pictured something like this happening in our neighborhood,” said neighbor Lilia Gaspar. Gaspar added, “I never would have pictured him doing something like this, I know he had a drinking problem, but I’ve known him for many years and I don’t know what could have gone through his mind.” Fortunately, none of the officers were injured. Chief Joseph stated that all three involved officers had several years of experience on the police force. The Santa Clara County District Attorney’s Office is investigating the shooting.

headlines.title: PG&E warns Bay Area customers of possible shutoffs amid high winds, dry conditions
headlines.description: Thousands of Pacific Gas and Electric customers across the Bay Area could lose power as early as Wednesday, including thousands in Alameda and Contra Costa counties. PG&E is concerned power lines could move or snap in the wind and spark a wildfire. The utility has posted a map online showing areas where customers have been notified about a potential Public Safety Power Shutoff. The shutoffs are expected to begin around 5:30 p.m. Wednesday and could last until Saturday afternoon. PG&E has warned 70,000 customers across 29 California counties that they are at risk of losing power, including more than 1,600 customers in Contra Costa County and more than 4,700 in Alameda County. Andrew McKoskey, who lives on Finley Road, is among the customers who received a text from PG&E warning that the power could be off for the next few days. For McKoskey, his pregnant wife and their 2-year-old son, the timing could be difficult. “Kinda lame because my wife’s about to go into labor,” McKoskey said. “Tomorrow’s her due date.” McKoskey said he hopes neighbors can help run the family’s generator while they are at the hospital so they don’t lose their food. “The reason we call these PSPS events is strictly for safety,” a PG&E spokesperson said. PG&E says early alerts give customers time to prepare, with possible outages lasting through Saturday afternoon. “We encourage you to be prepared now, start charging appliances and electronics, things like your electric vehicles or your phones,” said Tamar Sarkissian, a PG&E spokesperson. PG&E isn’t alone in taking precautions. Contra Costa fire officials are also monitoring the winds and plan to increase staffing if needed. “Anytime you have an offshore wind… the ability for fuel to lead to catastrophic fire danger,” said David Watson, assistant chief with the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District. PG&E says the areas affected could change depending on the weather. The utility is encouraging customers to check their address and sign up for alerts. Customers can look up their address online to find out if their location is being monitored for a potential safety shutoff at pge.com/pspsupdates. For more information on the possible PSPS, visit PG&E’s power shutoff forecast page.

headlines.title: Opening statements begin in Sheng Thao corruption trial
headlines.description: Opening statements began Wednesday in the federal corruption trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao, with prosecutors and the defense presenting two different accounts of the case. Opening statements have included references to alleged text messages, pictures, recordings and other evidence involving the four defendants. Thao arrived at the courthouse Wednesday morning with her attorney for the first day of what is expected to be a six-week trial. Her longtime partner and co-defendant, Andre Jones, arrived separately, as did the two other defendants, father-and-son businessmen David and Andy Duong. Prosecutors presented their case first, spending about an hour laying out their allegations. “This is a case about a public official who put her power up for sale,” prosecutors told the jury. Thao won a seat on the Oakland City Council in 2018 and narrowly won the race for mayor in 2023 by fewer than 700 votes. Prosecutors referenced that election and her victory during opening statements, including connections between the Duongs and Thao’s campaign. Sheng Thao 5 hours ago Sheng Thao 18 hours ago Sheng Thao Oct 13 Before the trial began, NBC Bay Area’s Investigative Unit reviewed court documents detailing evidence in the case. There have been 1,800 pieces of evidence submitted, including taped meetings that prosecutors are using in an attempt to establish a financial connection between Thao, her partner and the Duongs. The defense began its opening statements Wednesday morning, immediately disputing the account laid out by prosecutors. NBC Bay Area’s Ginger Conejero Saab has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: San Jose parents charged with child neglect in fatal asthma death of 8-year-old daughter
headlines.description: A San Jose mother and her husband appeared in court Tuesday to face multiple counts of child neglect in connection with the fatal asthma death of 8-year-old Aurora Williams. Gabrielle Hanson and Jacob Randolph did not enter a plea during their court appearance at the Hall of Justice regarding the May incident. According to court records, Aurora was in medical distress during her asthma attack for at least eight hours before the couple sought medical attention. She later died from a lack of oxygen to the brain, and the medical examiner ruled her death a homicide. When investigators searched the couple’s home, they found six children living in squalor, court documents show. Authorities reported there was no inhaler at the residence and that Aurora’s respirator was unusable because it was filled with cockroaches. “This little girl was filled with roaches, and there was also mold in the home, animal feces, and two parents who were not providing care or food for children,” said Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen. Prosecutors have also filed charges against Hanson’s brother, Jonathan Hansen, who was living in the same home. “We are also prosecuting Jonathan Hansen, Aurora’s uncle, and who was living in the same home, for sexually abusing and molesting one of Aurora’s siblings,” Rosen said. In the wake of the case, the district attorney is calling on Santa Clara County to do more to protect children by increasing involvement across multiple agencies. “This is a plan that would create a team of specialists who would work jointly to protect the most vulnerable like Aurora,” Rosen said.

headlines.title: SFUSD commissioners vote on ending school choice lottery in favor of neighborhood models
headlines.description: San Francisco Unified School District commissioners are voting Tuesday night on how to officially end the district’s school choice lottery program, deciding between two options that prioritize keeping students in the neighborhoods where they live. For the last 15 years, families with school-age children in San Francisco have had sometimes stressful starts to each school year because they have to rank their choice of campuses to attend. Parents have complained when schools in their neighborhoods are unavailable or when children in the same family get sent to different campuses. “The lottery is long maligned. No one is in favor of keeping the current lottery, it causes stress for everyone,” said Rebecca Kee, executive director of the San Francisco Parents Coalition. The group recently conducted a survey for feedback on the two options board commissioners will be considering tonight. The first option allows students to attend a school in their neighborhood and includes the option to apply to a school in a different neighborhood if there’s a seat available there. The second also allows students to go to school in their own neighborhood, or they can apply to a different campus, but only if that school has some kind of specialized program. Kee says parents they surveyed preferred the first of those options. “All of these options moving forward are focused on both giving parents a little bit more certainty and peace of mind in the process. But also, the opportunity to have choice and speak up for their child as well,” Kee said. District leaders had been considering three options. In working sessions with parents over the last few months, the superintendent and staff have gone over the details of all of them. “What we are going to do is share with our board and community the tradeoffs that we have to face,” SFUSD Superintendent Maria Su, Ph.D., said during a September 1 session. However, parents in some neighborhoods are raising concerns about what kind of zones will be considered as the district decides what constitutes a neighborhood. Coleman Advocates for Children, which works with Latine, Pacific Islander, and Indigenous families, raised concerns about a possible return to under-resourced schools in certain neighborhoods. A statement from the group reads in part: “Our communities have experienced school assignment policies, desegregation efforts, busing, school choice and other system changes in ways that have not always distributed the benefits or burdens equally.” After tonight’s vote, the details on those neighborhoods will still need to be worked out. The chosen option is expected to be implemented in 2028.

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax (not assigned) Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website.
